firstDays.title: First Days at Home
firstDays.q1: How do I prepare my home for a new pet?
firstDays.a1: Prepare the space in advance: bed, bowls, toys. Remove all dangerous objects and plants. Provide a quiet, safe place to rest. Give them time to adjust during the first days.
firstDays.q2: How much time is needed for adjustment?
firstDays.a2: Usually 2-4 weeks are needed, but this can vary by animal. Be patient and consistent. It's normal if they're shy or overactive during the first days.

nutrition.title: Nutrition
nutrition.q1: What should I feed my new pet?
nutrition.a1: During the first weeks, use the same food they received at the shelter, gradually transition to a new diet. Always have fresh water available. Ask your vet for advice on proper nutrition.
nutrition.a2: Dogs: 2-3 times daily. Cats: 2-4 smaller portions daily. Puppies/kittens: more frequently, 3-4 times. Follow portion guidelines to avoid overfeeding.

health.title: Healthcare
health.a1: Dogs: rabies, combination vaccine (distemper, parvo, hepatitis). Cats: rabies, feline flu, panleukopenia. Consult with your vet about the vaccination schedule.
health.q2: When should I take my pet to the vet?
health.a2: First visit: within 1-2 weeks of adoption for a general checkup. Regular: 1-2 times annually. Immediately: if you notice any unusual symptoms (vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, lethargy).
health.a3: Yes, very important! External parasites (fleas, ticks): monthly. Internal parasites (worms): every 3-6 months. Ask your vet about the appropriate products.

training.title: Training and Behavior
training.a1: Be consistent with all family members. Use positive reinforcement (reward good behavior). Never use physical punishment. Start immediately, don't delay.
training.q2: What should I do if behavioral problems occur?
training.a2: First try to understand the cause. Provide enough exercise and mental stimulation. Consult a behaviorist or trainer for serious problems. Be patient, change takes time.
training.a3: Extremely important, especially for puppies/kittens! Introduce them to other animals, people, environments. Careful, gradual introduction. Associate positive experiences with new situations.
